suggestions.rationale: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-15 adds this relationship only as the user-approved bounded clinical proposition. A nationally representative survey found panic disorder commonly co-occurs with agoraphobia in a minority of lifetime panic disorder cases, with the combination marking the most severe presentations; the approved relationship is limited to population-level co-occurrence risk and does not assert that panic disorder inevitably progresses to agoraphobia. Require independently documented panic disorder and separately established agoraphobia; under DSM-5 these are distinct diagnoses and agoraphobia must not be inferred from panic attacks or panic disorder alone. The cited nationally representative survey found that most lifetime panic disorder cases did not carry agoraphobia; do not present co-occurrence as inevitable progression. Preserve other anxiety disorders, depressive disorders, substance use, medical causes of episodic symptoms, and avoidance attributable to other conditions as competing explanations. Treat this only as population-level co-occurrence risk, not proof that panic disorder caused an individual's agoraphobia. The cited literature supports only this constrained proposition and does not, by itself, establish an individual medical nexus.
